      "body": "**FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**\n\nState after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements \u2014 Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):\n\n- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C \u22d9 forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman \u00a74 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.\n- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` \u2014 no defeq walls anywhere in this file).\n- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) \u2014 `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.\n\n**Caveat 1 \u2014 pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/\u00e9tale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now \u2014 record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.\n\n**Caveat 2 \u2014 `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free \u2124/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, \u00e9tale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient \u27e8sorry\u27e9` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only. Do NOT reintroduce a global instance, and do NOT try to prove the theorem as stated.",

          "body": "**Hygiene audit (janitor, 2026-07-25): the state snapshot in this memory is stale, but both caveats remain load-bearing \u2014 keeping open.**\n\nRe-checked `AJC/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean` at HEAD:\n\n- The file now has **exactly one** code `sorry`: the conditional `instHasPicScheme` under `[HasRationalPoint C]` (the genuine FGA existence statement).       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. section Coproduct

/-- **`FiniteInAffine` is closed under arbitrary set-indexed coproducts.**  If every
component scheme `g i` satisfies `FiniteInAffine`, so does `∐ g`.

A finite `s ⊆ ∐ g` meets only the finitely many components indexed by `idx '' s`; within
each, `s` pulls back along the open immersion `Sigma.ι g i` to a finite set covered by an
affine open `U i`; the images `Sigma.ι g i ''ᵁ U i` are pairwise disjoint
(`disjoint_opensRange_sigmaι`) affine opens (image of an affine open under an open
immersion), so their finite `iSup` is affine (`IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint`) and
contains `s`.

This is the property `§5.5`'s refutation identified as the one the degree-graded Picard
scheme has and global projectivity does not. -/
theorem finiteInAffine_sigma {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] (g : σ → Scheme.{u})
    (h : ∀ i, FiniteInAffine (g i)) : FiniteInAffine (∐ g) := by
  classical
  letI : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion (Sigma.ι g i) := fun i =>
    Scheme.IsLocallyDirected.instIsOpenImmersionι (Discrete.functor g) { as := i }
  intro s hs
  have hcomp : ∀ x : (∐ g : Scheme.{u}), ∃ i, x ∈ Set.range (Sigma.ι g i).base := by
    intro x
    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := (sigmaOpenCover g).exists_eq x
    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
  choose idx hidx using hcomp
  have hpre : ∀ i : σ, ((Sigma.ι g i).base ⁻¹' s).Finite := fun i =>
    hs.preimage ((Sigma.ι g i).isOpenEmbedding.injective).injOn
  choose U hU using fun i => h i _ (hpre i)
  set J : Set σ := idx '' s with hJ
  have hJfin : J.Finite := hs.image idx
  refine ⟨⟨⨆ i ∈ J, (Sigma.ι g i) ''ᵁ (U i).1, ?_⟩, ?_⟩
  · apply IsAffineOpen.biSup_of_disjoint hJfin
    · intro i _
      exact (U i).2.image_of_isOpenImmersion _
    · intro i _ j _ hij
      exact Disjoint.mono (Scheme.Hom.image_le_opensRange _ _)
        (Scheme.Hom.image_le_opensRange _ _) (disjoint_opensRange_sigmaι g i j hij)
  · intro x hx
    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hidx x
    have hyU : y ∈ (U (idx x)).1 := by
      apply hU (idx x)
      simp only [Set.mem_preimage, hy]
      exact hx
    have hmem : x ∈ (Sigma.ι g (idx x)) ''ᵁ (U (idx x)).1 := ⟨y, hyU, hy⟩
    exact (le_iSup₂ (f := fun i _ => (Sigma.ι g i) ''ᵁ (U i).1) (idx x)
      ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩) hmem

/-- A coproduct of schemes that are projective over one affine base satisfies
`FiniteInAffine`. This is the degree-piece bridge: projectivity is checked on
each component, while `FiniteInAffine` is concluded for their possibly infinite
coproduct. -/
theorem finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjective
    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsProjective) :
    FiniteInAffine (∐ fun i => (X i).left) :=
  finiteInAffine_sigma _ fun i => finiteInAffine_of_isProjective (hX i)

/-- A coproduct of H-quasi-projective schemes over one affine base satisfies
`FiniteInAffine`, even when the coproduct itself is not quasi-compact. -/
theorem finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isHQuasiProjective
    {σ : Type v} [Small.{u, v} σ] {S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S]
    (X : σ → Over S) (hX : ∀ i, (X i).hom.IsHQuasiProjective) :
    FiniteInAffine (∐ fun i => (X i).left) :=
  finiteInAffine_sigma _ fun i => finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjective (hX i)

/-- The carried very-ample form of `finiteInAffine_sigma_of_isProjective`.
At `Scheme.{0}`, `IsProjectiveWith` records a line bundle together with its
closed immersion into relative projective space; forgetting those certificates
piecewise gives `FiniteInAffine` for the coproduct. -/

import AlgebraicJacobian.Descent.SemilinearAction
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.Affine

/-!
# Finite subsets in affine opens

`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` is the action-free geometric condition behind the
finite-Galois quotient construction: every finite subset of `X` lies in one
affine open.  For a finite Galois extension, this immediately supplies
`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` for every action on `X`.

The property is stated independently of Picard data.  In particular, it is a
conclusion to be proved for a representing scheme, not an additional field of
the representability datum.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory
open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

/-- Every finite subset of a scheme is contained in a single affine open. -/
def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1

/-- An affine scheme satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    FiniteInAffine X :=
  fun _ _ ↦ ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩, fun _ _ ↦ trivial⟩

/-- `FiniteInAffine` is invariant under isomorphism. -/
theorem finiteInAffine_of_iso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ≅ Y)
    (h : FiniteInAffine X) : FiniteInAffine Y := by
  intro s hs
  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (e.hom.base ⁻¹' s)
    (hs.preimage (TopCat.homeoOfIso ((Scheme.forgetToTop).mapIso e)).injective.injOn)
  refine ⟨⟨e.hom ''ᵁ U.1, U.2.image_of_isOpenImmersion e.hom⟩, ?_⟩
  intro y hy
  exact ⟨e.inv.base y, hU (by simpa using hy), by simp⟩

/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along an affine morphism. -/
theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [IsAffineHom f] (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
  intro s hs
  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)
  exact ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1, U.2.preimage f⟩, fun x hx ↦ hU ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩⟩

/-- An object affine over a field spectrum satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
theorem finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsAffineHom X.hom] :
    FiniteInAffine X.left :=
  haveI := isAffine_of_isAffineHom X.hom
  finiteInAffine_of_isAffine _

/-- `FiniteInAffine` supplies the orbit condition for every finite-Galois
semilinear action on the scheme. -/
theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (h : FiniteInAffine X) :
    rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen where
  exists_affineOpen x := by
    obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
      h (Set.range fun gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L ↦ (rho.act gamma).hom.base x)
        (Set.finite_range _)
    exact ⟨U, fun gamma ↦ hU ⟨gamma, rfl⟩⟩

end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtPointedReduction
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.ProjectiveMorphism
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.CurveProjectivity
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.AmbientPicNotProper
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.StableAffineCover

/-!
# Quasi-projectivity, as the vocabulary `FiniteInAffine` was standing in for

`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`) says every finite
subset of `X` lies in a single affine open.  It is the elementary, action-free form
of the EGA II 4.5.4 hypothesis that the whole finite-Galois-quotient engine runs
on, and up to now the project carried it **by hand**, with the same sentence
written in three places: *"it holds for quasi-projective `X`, but mathlib has no
quasi-projectivity vocabulary at this pin, so for the curve it must be supplied by
hand"* (`Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean`,
`Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup.lean`, `Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`).

This file removes the hand: it derives `FiniteInAffine` from the project's
finite-projective-space notion `Scheme.Hom.IsHQuasiProjective`; projectivity is
the closed-immersion special case.  The chain is

  graded prime avoidance  ⟹  `FiniteInAffine (Proj 𝒜)`
                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine ℙ(n; S)`   (affine morphism descent)
                          ⟹  `FiniteInAffine X` for `X` H-quasi-projective over `S`.

## The two avoidance inputs

The original deep input is the first step, and it is **absent from mathlib
`v4.31`**: there is no *graded* prime avoidance.  Mathlib has
`Ideal.subset_union_prime_finite` — a homogeneous ideal not contained in the union
of finitely many primes is not contained in any one of them — but the element it
produces is an arbitrary element of the ideal, while
`AlgebraicGeometry.Proj.isAffineOpen_basicOpen` demands `f ∈ 𝒜 m` with `0 < m`.
Getting a **homogeneous** avoiding element of **positive degree** is §1, and it is
where the grading is consumed.

For a closed immersion the final transport is cheap: `IsClosedImmersion →
IsAffineHom`, and `IsAffineOpen.preimage` pulls affine opens back.  An open
immersion needs a second prime-avoidance step: after placing the finite image in
an affine open, `GaloisDescent.exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite` shrinks it to a
basic open lying inside the immersion range.  The standard closed/open
factorization then gives transport along every immersion.

Thus graded avoidance is the new algebraic result in this file.  Open-immersion
transport is the only additional substantive geometric step; its algebra is
delegated to the already-landed finite prime-avoidance theorem.  The remaining
H-quasi-projective and coproduct declarations are factorization and packaging.

## What this does and does not buy

It does **not** discharge the `FiniteInAffine` conjunct of
`Scheme.PointedPicSharpRep`.  That conjunct is about the **Picard scheme**, and
nothing in this project produces an H-quasi-projective witness for the relevant
Picard component.  Kleiman §5 `th:qpp&p` gives quasi-projectivity of `Pic^0`;
formalizing and transporting that source theorem remains open.  What changes is the *kind* of thing
that is open: the antecedent's last non-projection conjunct is now reducible to a
standard geometric hypothesis with a standard proof, rather than an elementary
condition invented here.  Stated as
`Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isHQuasiProjective` in §3.

It **does** discharge, unconditionally and for free, the orbit hypothesis of the
Galois-descent engine at every projective scheme
(`Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_isProjective`), which is what
`Picard/GaloisQuotientNonVacuity.lean` had only for *affine* `X` and what the
Albanese lane's `OrbitsInAffineOpen` had for no `X` at all.  Smooth proper
geometrically integral curves **are** projective in this project
(`AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.isProjective_of_smoothProperGeometricallyIntegral`,
`Picard/CurveProjectivity.lean`), so §3 fires at the curve itself with no
hypothesis beyond its own binders.

## What §5 is NOT: read this before consuming `PointedPicSharpRepProjective`

§5 restates the seam's antecedent with `IsProjective` of the representing scheme in
place of `FiniteInAffine`.  **That antecedent is refuted at the object it is about**,
and the refutation is landed here as a theorem, not left as prose:
`Scheme.not_isProjective_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover`.  Projectivity over a field
forces `IsProper`, hence `UniversallyClosed`, hence — over the compact `Spec k` —
`CompactSpace` (`Scheme.compactSpace_of_isProjective`); and the full Picard scheme is a
**disjoint union over `deg ∈ ℤ`** (Kleiman §6 `ex:curves`), which is not quasi-compact.
So `PointedPicSharpRepProjective` is not the standard hypothesis restated — it is
strictly stronger and false at `Pic_{C/k}`.

This is verbatim the trap `Picard/AmbientPicNotProper.lean` exists to record, "trap (c):
a `P → Q` whose antecedent is unsatisfiable in the intended setting", and it is caught by
that file's own theorems.  Kleiman's `th:qpp&p` gives quasi-projectivity of `Pic^0`,
not projectivity of the ambient scheme.  §5 therefore survives only as a
*conditional* reduction with an explicitly refuted antecedent; §3 and §4, which do not
mention the ambient Picard scheme, are unaffected.

An earlier revision of this section said §5 states the seam "with no condition invented
in this project anywhere in it".  Both halves were wrong: `Scheme.Hom.IsProjective` is
project-local (`Picard/ProjectiveMorphismBasic.lean`, mathlib `v4.31` has no
morphism-level projectivity at all), as are `PicScheme.picSharp` and
`Scheme.HasRationalPoint`; and the antecedent is not merely non-standard but refutable.

/-!
# The identity component of the Picard scheme

Let `G` be a `k`-group scheme locally of finite type. Its **identity
component** `G⁰` is the connected component of `|G|` containing the image of
the identity section. It is an open and closed subgroup scheme of `G`, of
finite type and geometrically irreducible over `k`, and its formation
commutes with extension of the base field (Kleiman, §5, Lem.~`lem:agps`).

This file develops that substrate for an arbitrary `k`-group scheme (§1) and
then specialises it to the conditional legacy `PicSharp` representer
`PicScheme C` (§2). Section §3 contains only candidate integer maps at the
trivial legacy test object; it does not construct the arbitrary-test degree on
the étale-sheafified Picard functor. The corresponding degree-zero
characterisation in §4 remains open and is not faithfully typed by its legacy
approximation.

## Main results

- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent` — the identity component
  `G⁰` of a `k`-group scheme `G` locally of finite type, as a `k`-scheme (an
  object of `Over (Spec k)`): the open subscheme of `G` carried by the
  connected component of the image of the identity section.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isOpenSubgroupScheme` —
  the inclusion `G⁰ ↪ G` is both an open and a closed immersion.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isSubgroupHomomorphism` —
  `G⁰` inherits the group-object structure of `G`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.baseChangeIso` — for a
  field extension `K/k`, the base change `(G⁰)_K` is isomorphic to `(G_K)⁰`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.GroupScheme.IdentityComponent.isFiniteTypeGeometricallyIrreducible`
  — `G⁰` is of finite type and geometrically irreducible over `k`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme` — the identity component
  `Pic⁰_{C/k}` of the Picard scheme.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.degree` — a conditional totalisation of
  an additive candidate at the legacy trivial test object, available only from
  `[ClassDegreePinned C]` and set arbitrarily to `0` off sections.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme.finrank_eq_genus` — the dimension of
  `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is the genus of `C`.
- `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Pic0Scheme.kPoints_iff_kerDegree` — the current
  conditional, typed-sorry approximation to the degree-zero characterisation;
  it is not an exact encoding of the classical statement on `k`-points.

The abelian-variety identification of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (smooth, proper,
geometrically irreducible `k`-group scheme of dimension `g(C)`) is assembled
in the sibling file `Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`.

## Remaining obligations

The §1 substrate for an abstract `k`-group scheme is unconditional. The open
residues downstream of arbitrary-field étale Picard representability are
mathematically distinct:

- a genuine signed family degree: an additive natural transformation whose
  fibre value is `χ(C_t, L_t) - χ(C_t, O_{C_t})`, locally constant on arbitrary
  test schemes and invariant under the relative Picard quotient. The existing
  `ClassDegreePinned` interface does not provide these properties.
- `Pic0Scheme.finrank_eq_genus`: the equality
  `dim Pic⁰_{C/k} = dim_k H¹(C, O_C) = g(C)`, which follows from
  Picard smoothness plus the tangent-space/dimension comparison. It does not
  depend on extracting a representing line bundle from a `k`-point.
- `Pic0Scheme.kPoints_iff_kerDegree`: the identification of the `k`-points of
  the legacy `Pic⁰_{C/k}` approximation with candidate-value-zero classes;
  its current type is not the arbitrary-field mathematical statement.

## References

- Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_IdentityComponent.tex`.
- Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §5, Lem.~`lem:agps` (identity component
  substrate) + Prp.~`prp:pic0` (specialisation to `Pic_{C/k}`) +
  Thm.~`th:qpp&p` (quasi-projectivity/projectivity) + Cor.~`cor:sm`
  (smoothness/dimension) + Ex.~`ex:jac` + Rmk.~`rmk:Jac`
  (arXiv:math/0504020 pp. 36, 38, 47, 50–51);
- Milne, "Abelian Varieties" (course notes, 2008), §III.1
  (def. of abelian variety, p. 8; dimension equals genus, Rmk. III.1.4(e),
  p. 86).
-/

     8	/-!
     9	# The finite-stage Picard glue as a scheme over its field of definition
    10	
    11	The finite-stage glue package already contains affine algebras over its final finite
    12	subextension `P.N.1`.  Their structure maps agree on overlaps, so they descend to the
    13	glued scheme.  This retains the finite-stage object over `Spec P.N.1`, which is the
    14	object-level input for the scalar-extension comparison with the separably closed atlas.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits TensorProduct
    22	open scoped TensorProduct
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    25	
    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    29	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    30	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    31	
    32	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    33	
    34	set_option linter.style.setOption false

    36	-- Projecting the dependent scalar towers from `P` requires a larger local synthesis budget.
    37	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    38	/-- The structure map from the finite-stage glued scheme to its field of definition. -/
    39	noncomputable def gluedMap
    40	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    41	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    42	    P.glueData.glued ⟶ Spec (.of P.N.1) := by
    43	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
    44	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
    45	  let A : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u := fun U =>
    46	    Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U
    47	  let B : Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C -> Type u :=
    48	    fun U V =>
    49	      Pic0FiniteStageOverlapBaseChangeRing C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U V
    50	  let r : ∀ U V, A U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    51	    pic0FiniteStageRestrictionBaseChange
    52	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
    53	  letI : ∀ U V, Algebra (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    54	    pic0FiniteStageAlgebraOfMap (r U V)
    55	  letI : ∀ U V, IsScalarTower P.N.1 (A U) (B U V) := fun U V =>
    56	    pic0FiniteStageTowerOfMap (r U V)
    57	  let tau : ∀ U V, B V U →ₐ[P.N.1] B U V := fun U V =>
    58	    pic0FiniteStageTransitionBaseChange
    59	      C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N U V
    60	  fapply Multicoequalizer.desc
    61	  · intro U
    62	    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U
    63	    exact Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U)))
    64	  · rintro ⟨U, V⟩
    65	    change Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C at U V
    66	    change
    67	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A U) (B U V))) ≫
    68	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A U))) =
    69	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (tau U V).toRingHom) ≫
    70	          Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (A V) (B V U)))) ≫
    71	            Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.N.1 (A V)))
    72	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    73	    rw [Category.assoc, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    74	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]

    78	      ConcreteCategory.hom_ofHom, RingHom.coe_comp, Function.comp_apply,
    79	      AlgHom.toRingHom_eq_coe, Category.assoc, RingHom.coe_coe]
    80	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A U) (B U V)]
    81	    rw [← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply P.N.1 (A V) (B V U)]
    82	    exact (tau U V).commutes x |>.symm

     8	/-!
     9	# Basic geometry of the finite-stage Picard glue
    10	
    11	The finite-stage glue is covered by finitely many affine spectra of explicit
    12	finite-presentation algebras over its field of definition.  Consequently its structure
    13	morphism is locally of finite type and quasi-compact, without any additional geometric
    14	hypothesis on the package.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory
    22	
    23	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	variable {k F : Type u} [Field k] [Field F]
    28	variable [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
    29	variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    32	
    33	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    34	
    35	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    36	-- The chart rings retain two nested finite-subextension tensor products.
    37	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    38	/-- The structure morphism of the finite-stage Picard glue is locally of finite type. -/
    39	theorem locallyOfFiniteType_gluedMap
    40	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    41	    LocallyOfFiniteType P.gluedMap := by
    42	  apply IsZariskiLocalAtSource.of_openCover P.glueData.openCover
    43	  intro U
    44	  change LocallyOfFiniteType (P.glueData.ι U ≫ P.gluedMap)
    45	  rw [glueData_ι_gluedMap C P U]
    46	  exact (HasRingHomProperty.Spec_iff (P := @LocallyOfFiniteType)).mpr
    47	    (RingHom.finiteType_algebraMap.mpr inferInstance)
    48	
    49	instance instLocallyOfFiniteTypeGluedMap
    50	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    51	    LocallyOfFiniteType P.gluedMap :=
    52	  locallyOfFiniteType_gluedMap C P
    53	
    54	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 3200000 in
    55	-- Unfolding the dependent affine glue identifies its finite spectrum charts.
    56	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    57	/-- The structure morphism of the finite-stage Picard glue is quasi-compact. -/
    58	theorem quasiCompact_gluedMap
    59	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    60	    QuasiCompact P.gluedMap := by
    61	  haveI : Finite P.glueData.openCover.I₀ := by
    62	    change Finite (Pic0FiniteStageChartIndex C)
    63	    infer_instance
    64	  haveI : ∀ U, CompactSpace (P.glueData.openCover.X U) := by
    65	    intro U
    66	    change CompactSpace
    67	      (Spec (CommRingCat.of
    68	        (Pic0FiniteStageChartBaseChangeRing
    69	          C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.N U)))
    70	    infer_instance
    71	  haveI : CompactSpace P.glueData.glued :=
    72	    P.glueData.openCover.compactSpace
    73	  exact (HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine (P := @QuasiCompact)).mpr
    74	    (inferInstance : CompactSpace P.glueData.glued)
    75	
    76	instance instQuasiCompactGluedMap
    77	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) :
    78	    QuasiCompact P.gluedMap :=
    79	  quasiCompact_gluedMap C P
    80	
    81	end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    82	
    83	end
    84	
    85	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	/-!
    11	# An inhabited finite-stage Picard glue package
    12	
    13	The simultaneous pair- and triple-transition descent theorems supply every input of
    14	`pic0FiniteStageAffineRingGlueData`.  This file records those dependent inputs in one
    15	package and immediately exposes the resulting scheme glue datum.
    16	-/
    17	
    18	set_option autoImplicit false
    19	
    20	universe u
    21	
    22	open CategoryTheory TensorProduct
    23	open scoped TensorProduct
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	noncomputable section
    28	
    29	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    30	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    31	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] [IsSepClosed k]
    32	
    33	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
    34	-- The fields retain three nested finite-subextension scalar towers.
    35	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
    36	/-- All finite-stage models and comparison equations needed to assemble the descended
    37	Picard atlas.  The fields are outputs of the simultaneous finite-subextension producers,
    38	not additional geometric hypotheses. -/
    39	structure Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    40	    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] where
    41	  L : DatG0.FinSubext F k
    42	  n : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat
    43	  m : Pic0FiniteStageRingIndex C -> Nat
    44	  relation : forall j, Fin (m j) -> MvPolynomial (Fin (n j)) L.1
    45	  e : forall j,
    46	    k ⊗[L.1] DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1 (n j) (m j) (relation j) ≃ₐ[k]
    47	      Pic0FiniteStageRing C j
    48	  M : DatG0.FinSubext L.1 k
    49	  mapM : forall q : Pic0FiniteStageMapIndex C,
    50	    Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
    51	        (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q) →ₐ[M.1]
    52	      Pic0FiniteStageModelRing C L n m relation M
    53	        (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q)
    54	  hmapM : forall q,
    55	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
    56	        (AlgHom.id L.1
    57	          (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
    58	            (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
    59	            (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))
    60	            (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapTarget C q))))).comp
    61	        ((mapM q).restrictScalars L.1) =
    62	      ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedMap C L n m relation e q).restrictScalars
    63	        L.1).comp
    64	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val
    65	          (AlgHom.id L.1
    66	            (DatG0.FiniteRelationAlgebra L.1
    67	              (n (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
    68	              (m (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q))
    69	              (relation (Pic0FiniteStageMapSource C q)))))
    70	  hOpen : forall i : Pic0FiniteStageRestrictionIndex C,
    71	    IsOpenImmersion
    72	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (mapM (Sum.inl i)).toRingHom))
    73	  N : DatG0.FinSubext M.1 k
    74	  thetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
    75	    N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
    76	        C L n m relation M mapM p →ₐ[N.1]
    77	      N.1 ⊗[M.1] Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
    78	        C L n m relation M mapM p
    79	  hthetaN : forall p : Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionIndex C,
    80	    (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
    81	        (AlgHom.id M.1
    82	          (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelTarget
    83	            C L n m relation M mapM p))).comp
    84	        ((thetaN p).restrictScalars M.1) =
    85	      ((pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels
    86	        C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2).restrictScalars
    87	          M.1).comp
    88	        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map N.1.val
    89	          (AlgHom.id M.1
    90	            (Pic0FiniteStageTripleTransitionModelSource
    91	              C L n m relation M mapM p)))
    92	
    93	namespace Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
    94	
    95	set_option maxHeartbeats 25600000 in
    96	-- The package projections retain the dependent tensor-product instances of the constructor.
    97	/-- The scheme glue datum computed from an inhabited finite-stage package. -/
    98	noncomputable def glueData
    99	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k]
   100	    (P : Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) : Scheme.GlueData := by
   101	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.L.1 k := by infer_instance
   102	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic P.M.1 k := by infer_instance
   103	  exact pic0FiniteStageAffineRingGlueData
   104	    C P.L P.n P.m P.relation P.M P.mapM P.N
   105	      P.e P.hmapM P.hOpen P.thetaN P.hthetaN
   106	
   107	end Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
   108	
   109	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 400000 in
   110	-- Selecting both finite families exposes many dependent quotient-algebra instances.
   111	set_option maxHeartbeats 12800000 in
   112	/-- The simultaneous finite-stage descent producers inhabit the glue package. -/
   113	theorem exists_pic0FiniteStageGluePackage
   114	    {F : Type u} [Field F] [Algebra F k] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F k] :
   115	    Nonempty (Pic0FiniteStageGluePackage C F) := by
   116	  classical
   117	  obtain ⟨L, n, m, relation, e, M, mapM, hmapM, hOpen, _⟩ :=
   118	    exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageTransition_models (C := C) (F := F)
   119	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic L.1 k := by infer_instance
   120	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic M.1 k := by infer_instance
   121	  let Q := pic0FiniteStageTripleModelComparisonFamily
   122	    C L n m relation e M mapM hmapM
   123	  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ :=
   124	    exists_finSubext_pic0FiniteStageTripleTransition_models_of_comparisons
   125	      C L n m relation M mapM Q
   126	  choose thetaN hthetaN using hN
   127	  exact ⟨{
   128	    L := L
   129	    n := n
   130	    m := m
   131	    relation := relation
   132	    e := e
   133	    M := M
   134	    mapM := mapM
   135	    hmapM := hmapM
   136	    hOpen := hOpen
   137	    N := N
   138	    thetaN := thetaN
   139	    hthetaN := by
   140	      intro p
   141	      simpa only [Q, pic0FiniteStageTransportedTripleTransitionOfModels] using
   142	        hthetaN p
   143	  }⟩
   144	
   145	end
   146	
   147	end AlgebraicGeometry
